title: Invertibility of a natural comparison on all shifts is localizing
statement: Let C and D be pretriangulated additive categories with integer shifts [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Let F,G:C→D have separately chosen coherent exact shift structures and let τ:F→G be any natural transformation. For a distinguished triangle A→B→C→A[1], invertibility of τ at A,B,A[1],B[1] implies invertibility at C. No shift-compatibility condition on τ is required. Consequently Q(X):=∀n∈ℤ, IsIso(τ_(X[n])) is closed under isomorphisms, shifts, retracts, distinguished triangles, and every coproduct preserved by F and G.

source.place: coyoneda_exact₁/₂/₃ and naturality; five-term diagram chase. The proved private cone_five_lemma is extracted from FlatTelescopeNormalizationUnshiftedIsIso, with attribution in the Lean header.

proof.text: Compare the Hom(A,-) sequences of two distinguished triangles. If the four outside components a,b,d,e are invertible, cancellation with d and exactness show the middle map c is mono. For any map y into the target third object, pull its connecting image back through d; cancellation with e shows it lies in the preceding kernel. Lift it by exactness, then correct the difference y-xc by a lift through b. Thus the Yoneda maps of c are bijective and c is invertible.

Apply this diagram chase to F(T) and G(T). Choose d to be F.commShiftIso(1).inv at A followed by τ_(A[1]) followed by G.commShiftIso(1).hom at A, and likewise e at B. Ordinary naturality of τ and of the functor shift isomorphisms proves all four squares.

Define Q using all integer shifts. Transport naturality along isomorphisms; conjugate using the shift-add isomorphism for shift closure; apply retractArrowApp for retracts. For coproducts whisker the coproduct diagram by the shift equivalence and use the invertibility of the transformation on a preserved colimit. Apply the preceding four-component lemma to the triangle shifted by n for each n to get triangle closure.
